prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat bands in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in it, opening the field of moire quantum materials

statement.case_for: I opened with B040 first, but having read all eight ballots I move B025 to the head of my configuration. It is the only candidate that appears on every ballot (three first places, four top-three, ranked by all eight members), and that breadth is informative rather than merely a count: members from AMO, condensed matter, quantum technology and computation each find the science compelling on its own terms. As an experimentalist I value the structure of the discovery. A continuum-model prediction of a magic angle (Bistritzer and MacDonald) was followed by a decisive experiment in which a single, gate-tunable control parameter produced correlated insulators and superconductivity (Jarillo-Herrero's group in 2018). That is a prediction-then-confirmation chain with a clean experimental signature, replicated by many independent groups within a few years, and it created a whole field of moire quantum materials. The citation can be stated in one sentence and the three-name theory-plus-experiment configuration is coherent, as Danielsson, Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson all independently proposed essentially the same trio.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is timing and attribution. The experiments date from 2018, and the microscopic mechanism of the superconductivity is still debated, so there is a real risk of honouring the phenomenon before its interpretation is settled; several colleagues, including Danielsson and Kroll, say as much. Attribution is also not clean: Eva Andrei's early scanning-probe evidence of flat bands and van Hove singularities at small twist angles is a credible competing claim that a three-name cap forces us to leave aside, and I am relying on the supplied ballots rather than a verified historical record for the priority question. By comparison B040 and B013 are older and have fully settled interpretations, so B025 is the choice that depends most on judging that the established core of the discovery is already robust enough.

responses.point: Johansson ranks B025 first but substitutes Eva Y. Andrei for Rafi Bistritzer, arguing that early STM evidence of flat bands is an earlier experimental contribution and that Bistritzer's role is the one to question.
responses.response: I disagree with that substitution. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model is the quantitative origin of the magic-angle concept that the 2018 experiments targeted; dropping one half of that theory pair leaves a prize with a prediction credited to one person and weakens the prediction-then-confirmation logic that makes the case persuasive. Andrei's work is genuinely important and I would not dismiss it, but it is an earlier observation of related band features rather than the discovery of the correlated and superconducting states. If the committee finds Andrei's claim stronger than I do, the honest alternative is to revisit the whole allocation, not to swap out one of the theory authors. I also note Johansson's own caution about proximity to circuit QED; I read that as a sign of care, and it does not change my view of B025.

responses.point: Danielsson places B033 (Kane, Molenkamp, Xue; quantum spin Hall and quantum anomalous Hall effects) first and B025 second, regarding B025 as possibly early because the superconducting mechanism is unresolved, and values the long theory-to-measurement chain of B033.
responses.response: I take the timing concern seriously and it is the main thing that keeps me from full confidence in B025. But I would separate the mechanism of superconductivity, which is open, from the existence of flat-band correlated insulators and gate-tunable superconductivity, which is not in doubt after eight years of replication. On B033 versus B013, I think bundling quantum spin Hall and the quantum anomalous Hall effect in one citation risks combining two separate discoveries; the topological-insulator line has wide support in this committee (B013 has four top-three rankings) and I would rather see that line considered as one coherent topic, with the credit question about Hasan and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal debated openly, than split between two ballots. That is why I keep B013 as my first alternative.

responses.point: Kroll ranks the optical lattice clock (B006, Katori and Ye) first as an original, clean, instrument-plus-concept discovery that is mature, independently confirmed and timely given the prospective redefinition of the second, and puts B025 only sixth as probably early.
responses.response: I share Kroll's appreciation for this kind of precision instrumentation, and I ranked B006 fifth for that reason; the two-name attribution is fair and the maturity is not in question. My reservation is about novelty relative to the earlier frequency-comb and ion-clock prizes: the committee would need to be convinced that the magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct discovery rather than a further refinement of recognised metrology. I do not think that objection is fatal, so I would not oppose B006 strongly, but it has fewer top-three placements than B025 or B013 and it is not the configuration I would lead with. Kroll's sixth-place ranking of B025 reflects the same timing worry as Danielsson's; I answer it with the replication record rather than by discounting it.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks B025 first as a case where band-structure engineering through one control parameter yields strongly correlated phases, and B013 second, accepting that leaving out Andrei is a real allocation difficulty but that the three-name theory-plus-experiment set is coherent.
responses.response: I agree with the scientific assessment and with the three-name set. Where I would add a qualification is on his comment that the field might be too young to single out one discovery from a family of moire effects. I think the answer is in the citation: it should be anchored on flat bands and the first correlated and superconducting states in magic-angle graphene, not on moire physics at large, so that later fractional Chern insulators and other platforms are neither claimed nor excluded. That scoping also helps with the credit question.

uncertainties: Whether Eva Y. Andrei's early scanning-probe contribution should be weighed against Bistritzer or another named laureate, which I cannot settle from the supplied ballots.
Whether the unresolved pairing mechanism makes B025 premature relative to B013, which is older and fully settled.
Whether B013 would be a better choice if the committee can resolve the Hasan and Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang credit problem.
Whether the single-name IceCube candidate (B008) can be rescued for a collaboration-scale discovery; I did not move it into my preferred configuration for that reason.
statement.conflict_note: As Chair I disclose documented connections to PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur and a research field in gamma-ray and hard-X-ray instrumentation. My opening first choice, B040 (gamma-ray burst afterglows), and B008 (IceCube) lie close to my own astroparticle and gamma-ray field, and Fermi-LAT observes gamma-ray bursts, so I flag possible proximity if either is taken forward and would be willing to step back from the discussion of B040 if colleagues think that appropriate. No specific personal or institutional tie to the named candidates in B025, the preferred configuration, is apparent from the provided profile.
